{"topic":"app-manual","bytes":1360,"guide":"## WORKFLOWS — start to finish: a script to a finished video, one picture to an ad, the same character in every shot, cheap previews first, letting an AI do it

### Workflow: keep a character or product the same in every shot (Library, @name, identity sheet, voice)

1. Save one clean picture of them to the Library: **More › Save to Library…** on the picture, or **New {Noun}** on a category page. For a character, an **Identity sheet** helps.
2. Write `@name` in every prompt that shows them. Their picture attaches as a numbered reference; See what gets sent shows the words the model receives.
3. For one look across the film, make a Looks item and write `#name` in each prompt.
4. Give a character a voice (their card → **Add voice**). On video models that take one, the voice attaches with the `@name`.
5. Check the reference rail before pressing **Generate**: a tile marked **Not sent** is past the model's limit.

Details: THE LIBRARY; "Prompt box: @ and # mentions, image 1 citations".

Related sections (ask by heading): Library: New dialog Generate form (character sheet, identity prompt, location prompt, style change, source images, Create & Generate) · Library: sheet tools (Identity sheet, Establishing image, turnaround, character sheet, price) · Videos · Prompt box: pick a model (model picker, search models, families, Face, tools)"}

Slates handles this through the **Library**. You save the character once, then call them by name in every prompt.

1. **Save one clean picture of them to the Library.** On a picture you like, open **More › Save to Library…**. Or start from scratch with **New Character** on the Characters page. Making an **Identity sheet** for them gives the models a better face reference.
2. **Write `@name` in every prompt they appear in**, for example `@Maya walks into the diner`. Their picture is attached to the prompt as a numbered reference. To check exactly what the model will receive, use **See what gets sent**.
3. **Keep the look consistent too (optional).** Make a **Looks** item and write `#name` in each prompt so the whole film shares one style.
4. **Give them a voice (optional).** On the character's card, click **Add voice**. Video models that accept a voice will pick it up automatically with the `@name`.
5. **Check the reference rail before you press Generate.** A tile marked **Not sent** means that model's reference limit has been reached, so that picture won't be used. Remove some references or switch models.

You'll get the most consistent face from a clear, well-lit, front-facing picture plus an identity sheet.

I can point out any of these controls on your screen, or look at your project's Library to check whether your character is already saved.
